data.title: FATF removes Bulgaria, Congo, Ivory Coast and Monaco from 'grey list' but leaves Vietnam on
data.description:
Key points:
  • FATF removes Bulgaria, Congo, Ivory Coast and Monaco from 'grey list'
  • Financial crime watchdog leaves Vietnam on 'grey list', expresses significant concern
  • Watchdog leaves Iran, Myanmar and North Korea on 'black list'

By Kanjyik Ghosh and Karin Strohecker

The world's top financial crime watchdog gave four countries a clean bill of health on Friday, taking Bulgaria, Ivory Coast, Democratic Republic of Congo and Monaco off its "grey list" — even as it put Vietnam on notice for dragging its feet on reform.

Landing on the grey list doesn't bring sanctions, but it does make life more costly: Banks and other financial institutions tend to scrutinise transactions more closely, which can dampen investment and capital flows.

As for Vietnam, the Financial Action Task Force was blunt: "The FATF will consider next steps if Vietnam does not make tangible improvements to rectify its strategic deficiencies by the next Plenary meeting."

On the four countries it removed from the list, the agency cited their "positive progress in addressing strategic anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism and proliferation financing deficiencies identified during their mutual evaluations."

The DRC's Finance Minister Doudou Roussel Fwamba Likunde Li-Botayi welcomed the decision.

"Removal from the list is expected to reduce the cost and friction of cross-border transactions for Congolese banks, businesses and citizens, support correspondent banking relationships," he said in a statement.

Monaco's minister of state Christophe Mirmand struck a similar note, calling it recognition of sustained effort: "This decision recognizes more than two years of concrete, rigorous and coordinated work by all of the State's authorities and departments."

MYANMAR, IRAN AND NORTH KOREA REMAIN ON 'BLACK LIST'

The agency left Iran and Myanmar on its "black list" of countries or jurisdictions with serious strategic deficiencies to counter money laundering, terrorist financing, and financing of proliferation.

The agency also renewed its push for Myanmar to crack down on the widespread fraud and scam operations running out of the country.

Earlier on Friday, Reuters reported that Japan had been lobbying the watchdog to remove Myanmar from the blacklist in hopes of smoothing the path for business there. Myanmar landed on the list in 2022 after the military coup sent the country spiralling into turmoil and civil war.

North Korea, too, stayed on the black list. Analysts have blamed hackers there for the theft of $6.3 billion from Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange — a heist some believe could be the biggest in financial history.

For years, Pyongyang has leaned on state-linked cyber units for espionage and to rake in revenue through financial theft, according to US and South Korean authorities as well as cybersecurity experts — allegations North Korea routinely denies.

Blacklisting is the harshest label FATF can hand out, and it has serious implications: frozen investments, soaring compliance costs, and banks effectively cut off from the global financial system.

data.title: Meta Stocks Edged Lower With Reporting and Product-Assessment Duties in Focus
data.description:
Meta Platforms , the parent of Facebook and Instagram, has another compliance hurdle to clear. Shares moved lower 0.74% to $619.88 at 12:30 p.m. ET on October 30 as a UK court rejected a challenge to Ofcom's information requests. The immediate burden is practical: gathering moderation records and producing the evidence the regulator wants.

The notices sought data on content removals and restrictions on visibility, according to Reuters reporting on the ruling. Separately, Ofcom opened an investigation on October 6 into Meta's illegal-content and children's risk assessments. Significant changes to how a service works can require fresh assessments, adding another step between building a feature and meeting regulatory requirements. Neither the response costs nor any resulting earnings impact has been quantified.

The financial snapshot offers some perspective. Meta carries a $1.58 trillion market value, trades at 21.14 times earnings and earns a GuruFocus GF Score of 99 out of 100, with profitability and growth its strongest displayed attributes. Those readings suggest considerable business strength, but they cannot settle the compliance question. The next test is whether Meta can meet the regulator's demands without adding meaningful costs or slowing product execution.

Mastercard Stocks Edged Higher With Revenue Outpacing Spending Volumes
data.description:
Mastercard , the global payments network, is turning spending growth into a bigger revenue payday. Shares rose 0.20% to $636.97 at 12:35 p.m. ET on October 30, following a quarter in which the company delivered strong growth as consumer spending held up. The investor question goes beyond how much cardholders spend: how much revenue can Mastercard capture from that activity?

Quarterly revenue climbed 14% to $9.8 billion, while gross dollar volume increased 7% in local currency and cross-border volume rose 11%. Adjusted operating margin reached 60.5%, up from 59.8% a year earlier. Revenue outpaced spending volume, and Mastercard kept more of it as operating profit. Still, that seven-percentage-point growth gap cannot be credited entirely to pricing; services, transaction mix and the different measurement bases also matter.

The valuation leaves Mastercard with something to prove. GuruFocus shows a GF Score of 98 out of 100, with profitability and growth standing out, alongside a price-to-earnings ratio of 35.04. That combination suggests investors are paying a premium for business quality, potentially leaving less room for disappointment. Services expansion, cross-border activity and margins could determine whether Mastercard keeps earning that premium if spending growth cools.

data.title: Trump admin again loses bid to block California from counting alleged noncitizen votes
data.description:
A US appeals court on Friday rejected the Trump administration's request that it temporarily block California from counting any mail ballots for the November 3 midterm elections from more than 20,000 registered voters the Trump administration alleges are likely noncitizens.

The decision marked the second time this week that the San Francisco-based 9th US Circuit Court of Appeals had denied an emergency request in the case from the Justice Department.

The decision comes as President Donald Trump's fellow Republicans are battling to retain majorities in both houses of Congress in the midterms. Trump's administration has sought to pressure state election officials over alleged noncitizen voting, which all available evidence shows is exceedingly rare.

On October 15, the Justice Department filed a lawsuit asking a federal judge to order California to separate any ballots it received from people on the administration's list of alleged noncitizens and to not count them until it had verified that the people who cast the ballots were citizens.

US District Judge David Carter denied the Trump administration's request for a temporary restraining order, writing on October 28 that it would "wreak havoc" on the election and potentially disenfranchise thousands of lawfully registered voters.

data.title: Tech rout drives gold to one-year low, white metals sink deep into oversold zone
data.description:
Key points:
  • Gold falls below key level of $4,000/oz
  • Silver slides below $50/oz for the first time in 11 months
  • Palladium slumps below $1,000/oz
  • RSI for silver, platinum, palladium is in oversold territory

By Noel John and Polina Devitt

Gold prices hit a one-year low on Friday while silver, platinum and palladium slid deep into technically oversold territory, as tech shares slumped amid worries that AI spending may not deliver sufficient returns.

Spot gold fell 3.5% to $3,880.97 an ounce by 2:13 p.m. ET (1813 GMT) — its lowest level since October 2025 — while silver dropped 6.5% to $49, breaking below $50 for the first time in 11 months, and palladium slid below $1,000.

US gold futures for December delivery settled 3.3% lower at $3,898.90 per ounce.

"The sky is falling," said independent metals trader Tai Wong. "Metals will not be able to escape the gravity well of a nasty stock correction. Earnings have been the foundation of the AI rally and now that pillar is showing some cracks."

Friday's sharp fall in technology stocks may have led to forced selling of safe-haven assets, such as gold, and margin calls, analysts at Commerzbank said in a note, adding that they expected a recovery in precious metals ahead.

Gold is down 30% since hitting a record high of $5,595 in January due to bets on interest rates staying higher for longer and is currently under pressure from muted demand in Asia. Analysts, however, say central bank demand tends to strengthen whenever gold is below $4,000.

Meanwhile, the three white precious metals - silver, platinum and palladium - lack the support that gold has received in recent years from purchases by central banks and safe-haven investment demand.

This week's 7% to 9% fall in silver, platinum and palladium, compared with a 2.9% decline in gold, took their Relative Strength Index deeply into the "oversold" zone for the first time in three years, signalling the strength of current bearish momentum.

"What is particularly troublesome for the white metals is that the downturn has been grinding and relentless rather than a sharp spike that is quickly recovered," Wong said.

Silver was increasingly viewed as an industrial growth-dependent commodity. HSBC said industrial and jewellery demand for silver was falling, and it expects an average silver price of $64 per ounce in 2027, down from its average forecast of $71 for silver this year.

To buy a single ounce of gold, one currently needs 79 ounces of silver (XAU-XAG), the most in 11 months, compared with 46 ounces in January, when silver hit a record high of $122.

From a historical perspective, silver still has room to fall further vs gold: this ratio, according to consultancy Metals Focus, averaged 82 in 2020 to 2025.

Platinum and palladium touched their lowest levels in 13 and 17 months respectively, with palladium slipping below $1,000 an ounce and the gold-platinum ratio (XAU-XPT) climbing to 2.7, the highest since mid-2025.

Platinum was last down 4.2% at $1,425.02, while palladium lost 3% to $976.08 under pressure from worries about auto sector demand.

data.title: BP's Blowout Quarter Comes With a Big Catch
data.description:
BP delivered a record third-quarter profit as stronger refining margins and higher energy prices boosted earnings, but management stopped short of increasing shareholder returns as it continues prioritizing debt reduction.

Underlying replacement cost profit reached $8.46 billion, comfortably beating analysts' expectations of $7.33 billion and jumping from $2.2 billion a year earlier. BP shares were roughly flat despite the record result.

The refining business was a major driver.

BP's refining indicator margin climbed to $46.70 per barrel, up from $29.60 in the second quarter and just $15.80 a year earlier. The company also reported significantly stronger gas marketing and trading results, while upstream production held at about 2.2 million barrels per day.

Cash generation was equally strong.

Operating cash flow came in at $14.8 billion, while net debt fell to $13.9 billion, allowing BP to reach its debt target roughly a year ahead of schedule.

Even so, CEO Meg O'Neill said BP still carries more debt than management is comfortable with under a lower-price scenario.

That is why the company is focusing on strengthening the balance sheet and protecting the existing dividend rather than increasing it or restarting share repurchases.

BP also took another hit from its low-carbon portfolio.

The company recorded about $4 billion of impairments during the quarter, largely tied to Lightsource BP and offshore wind. That follows more than $5 billion of recent write-downs across Lightsource BP, biogas business Archaea and other low-carbon investments.

Some of the surplus cash will also be used to settle remaining liabilities from the 2010 Deepwater Horizon disaster.

BP still carries about $5.94 billion of related payables and provisions, with payments scheduled through 2033.

Investor takeaway

I think the most important part of BP's quarter is the contrast between record earnings and unusually cautious capital returns.

BP clearly has the cash.

Refining margins are exceptional, operating cash flow is strong, and the company reached its debt target much earlier than expected.

But management is signaling that it does not want to treat today's elevated energy prices as permanent.

That is a conservative decision, and potentially a sensible one, but it also explains why the stock did not respond more enthusiastically to a record quarter.

For investors, the key things to watch are net debt, refining margins, low-carbon impairments, Deepwater Horizon payments and the December 15 strategy update.

BP has proven it can generate enormous cash in the current environment.

Now management has to show what the next growth phase actually looks like.

data.title: SpaceX Relies on Anthropic for a Third of Its Revenue
data.description:
SpaceX's largest customer is Anthropic, which accounted for 34.5% of the company's third-quarter revenue, Bloomberg reported, citing a person familiar with the matter. SpaceX shares were down 4.01% as of 10:00 a.m. ET.

SpaceX's quarterly filing identifies the buyer only as Customer B, whose revenue sits in the Super Intelligence segment, the AI computing unit that generated $7.56 billion of SpaceX's $14.58 billion in third-quarter revenue. Anthropic's payments have overtaken those from the U.S. federal government, previously SpaceX's largest customer, Bloomberg reported.

Anthropic has agreed to spend as much as $120.5 billion under computing contracts with SpaceX through 2029, about $3.1 billion a month starting in December, according to Bloomberg, citing Anthropic's IPO disclosures. The agreements allow Anthropic to terminate them with 90 days' notice from early 2027, the report said.

data.title: ADM Tronics Closes First Two Tranches of Private Placement and Strengthens Board of Directors
data.description:
NORTHVALE, NJ / ACCESS Newswire / October 30, 2026 / ADM Tronics Unlimited, Inc. ("ADM Tronics" or the "Company") today announces that on October 27, 2026, it completed an initial $1.3 million closing of a private placement of shares of common stock at a price of $0.10 per share, together with warrants to purchase a number of shares of common stock equal to 50% of the shares purchased. On October 28, 2026, the Company completed a second closing of $250,000 on the same terms, bringing aggregate gross proceeds from the private placement to date to approximately $1.55 million. The Company expects to raise approximately $5.0 million in the private placement, with the remaining amounts expected at one or more subsequent closings, subject to the satisfaction of customary closing conditions.

The Company also announced the appointment of new directors to its Board:

  • Klaus Kleinfeld, former Chairman and CEO of Siemens AG and Alcoa/Arconic, who will serve as Independent Non-Executive Chairman;
  • Greg Wasson, former President and CEO of Walgreens Boots Alliance; and
  • Michael Burychka, former CEO of IP Group plc's North American business.

Andre' DiMino will continue as a director, and ADM Tronics' existing medical device, chemical, and engineering services businesses will continue under his leadership as CEO. Michael Burychka's appointment took effect upon the initial closing. The appointments of Klaus Kleinfeld and Greg Wasson will take effect following the expiration of the ten-calendar-day period after the Company's information statement on Schedule 14F-1 has been both filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission and transmitted to stockholders.

Proceeds from the private placement will be used for working capital, transaction costs, and the development of new businesses in deep technology. The Company expects to provide further information on its plans in the coming months.

"This is a very positive transaction for our shareholders, many of whom have supported ADM Tronics for decades," said Andre' DiMino. "New investors are buying shares at a premium, and the Company gains new capital, new opportunities and an exceptional Board. I will continue to manage our existing businesses; our customers and employees can count on that."

"I've spent my career leading businesses alongside great teams, and the first thing I look for is people who know how to execute," said Greg Wasson, Co-Founder of Wasson Enterprise, which acts for the anchor investor group in the private placement. "The leadership and Board coming together bring exactly that. Wasson Enterprise believes in the collective team we're bringing to this opportunity, and we're proud to support it."

"I'm pleased to join the Board and look forward to working with my fellow directors as we develop new opportunities to grow shareholder value," said Klaus Kleinfeld.

Further details are in the Company's Current Report on Form 8-K, filed today with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

The securities sold and to be sold in the private placement have not been registered under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, or any state securities laws, and may not be offered or sold in the United States absent registration or an applicable exemption from registration. ADM Tronics Unlimited, Inc. is a technology-based company with operations in medical electronic devices, water-based chemical formulations, and FDA-registered engineering and contract manufacturing services. data.title: ExxonMobil Stocks Move Higher With Cash Covering Quarterly Payouts Twice
data.description:
ExxonMobil , the integrated oil and gas producer, has plenty of cash behind its payouts. Shares rose 1.43% to $185.92 at 12:45 p.m. ET on October 30 as a refining earnings surge helped power shareholder returns. The bigger draw for investors: cash generation comfortably outpaced dividends and buybacks, giving the company room to fund both without exhausting its quarterly free cash flow.

ExxonMobil's quarterly filing reported $25.7 billion in operating cash flow and $19.1 billion in free cash flow, against $4.3 billion in dividends and $5.1 billion in repurchases. That puts free cash flow at roughly twice the combined $9.4 billion payout, leaving about $9.7 billion before other financing uses. Adjusted earnings reached $17.5 billion, with Energy Products contributing approximately $9.1 billion, or 52%. That contribution also creates a pressure point: softer refining margins could take a meaningful bite out of earnings.

The valuation leaves investors something to weigh. GuruFocus shows a price-to-earnings ratio of 23.92 and a GF Score of 71 out of 100, with financial strength and profitability standing above growth, momentum and GF Value on its dashboard. That combination suggests the financial cushion looks stronger than the valuation appeal. ExxonMobil has demonstrated that it can cover substantial distributions this quarter; sustaining that cushion as refining conditions change could be the tougher test.

data.title: AstraZeneca Stocks Rise 7.65% With $2 Billion Restructuring Cost Ceiling
data.description:
AstraZeneca , the global drugmaker, is putting a $2 billion restructuring bill behind its next growth push. Shares climbed 7.65% to $187.75 at 12:40 p.m. ET on October 30 as Reuters reported a spending overhaul alongside quarterly results. The prize is $1.5 billion in annualized pretax benefits. The bigger question: how much growth can that money buy?

The company's results announcement puts one-time restructuring costs at up to $2 billion, with savings earmarked for reinvestment, principally in its development pipeline. September-quarter revenue reached $16.21 billion, up 7% at constant currencies, while full-year guidance stayed unchanged. That makes this a bet on future medicines, with the earnings benefit depending on when savings arrive and how quickly the company spends them.

The valuation leaves room for scrutiny. GuruFocus shows a GF Score of 79 out of 100 and a price-to-earnings ratio of 28.06, with profitability and GF Value scoring more strongly than momentum. The sharp daily gain therefore sits alongside a weaker momentum reading. At the targeted annual benefit, the maximum restructuring bill equals roughly 1.3 years of gross savings, but that calculation excludes reinvestment and implementation timing. Investors now need evidence that the spending shift can turn promising late-stage programs into commercial returns.

data.title: Oil's Latest Surge Threatens Another Shock to American Budgets
data.description:
Oil prices climbed Friday and were on track for a fourth consecutive monthly gain after a tanker attack in the Strait of Hormuz intensified concerns that the U.S.-Iran conflict could disrupt one of the world's most important energy chokepoints.

Brent crude for December rose about 2% to $117.14 a barrel, while the more actively traded January contract gained to $113.10.

West Texas Intermediate crude climbed roughly 1.9% to $103.94.

For October, Brent was headed for a gain of about 13%, while WTI was on pace to rise roughly 15%.

The immediate catalyst was an attack on a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, the key sea route for Gulf crude and refined fuels.

The vessel was struck by explosive devices attached by a small boat, according to the UK Maritime Trade Operations. It was not immediately clear who carried out the attack.

Maritime sources said it was the first known successful use of limpet mines in the waterway since the U.S. war with Iran began in February.

That matters because the market is already becoming more nervous about what could happen after the U.S. midterm elections.

Saxo Bank commodity strategist Ole Hansen said investors are increasingly concerned that U.S. attacks on Iran could resume after the vote.

The region is also seeing broader signs of escalation.

Iranian-backed Houthi militants said Thursday they attacked multiple sites in Saudi Arabia, including Ras Tanura, the Rabigh refinery and a production facility at Abqaiq. A Saudi-led coalition separately said it intercepted a cruise missile aimed at the kingdom's western region.

Diplomatic efforts are still continuing.

Qatari mediators returned to Tehran on Friday, while U.S. Vice President JD Vance has reportedly reached out to Iran in an effort to restart talks.

But Iran has so far remained cautious about the chances of a near-term agreement.

Security concerns are already affecting corporate behavior as well, with ExxonMobil and Chevron executives reportedly canceling plans to attend a major oil industry event in the United Arab Emirates next week.

data.title: Reynolds Wrap® debuts Snowflakes Fun Foil® ahead of holiday baking and entertaining
data.description:
Limited-edition design brings a festive touch to holiday celebrations, gifting, and creative projects

LAKE FOREST, Ill., Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Reynolds Wrap® is expanding its Fun Foil® portfolio with the introduction of Reynolds Wrap® Snowflakes Fun Foil®, a limited-edition aluminum foil featuring an embossed snowflake design. Available for the holiday season, the new offering combines a festive seasonal pattern with the quality and performance consumers have trusted from Reynolds Wrap® for more than 75 years.

Designed for a variety of holiday uses, Snowflakes Fun Foil® can be used to cover dishes for gatherings, package homemade treats, store leftovers, wrap handcrafted gifts, and create winter-themed crafts and art projects.

"The holidays are filled with opportunities to create, celebrate and connect with others," said Nancy Gannon, Marketing Director of Reynolds Wrap and Bakeware. "Whether used for wrapping baked treats, gift giving, cookie exchanges, decorating, or crafting, Snowflakes Fun Foil® helps consumers add a festive touch to the moments, traditions, and projects that make the season so special."

Reynolds Wrap® Snowflakes Fun Foil® is available nationwide online at Walmart.com and Amazon.com, and in stores at Walmart, Kroger, and other retailers. For more information on Reynolds Wrap® Snowflakes Fun Foil® visit: https://www.reynoldsbrands.com/whats-new/fun-foil-snowflakes-pattern
